title: Uptime sprint stitching playbook for feature launches
content:
Executive summary:
This playbook captures a 6- to 12-week ‘stitching’ approach to align product, platform, SRE, observability, and customer-facing teams for high-risk feature launches. It focuses on (1) clear SLO commitments for the feature surface, (2) telemetry readiness, (3) capacity and chaos rehearsal, and (4) an explicit fallback and rollout pattern.

Outcome we are optimizing for:
- Keep feature-specific error budget consumption below 2% of total service budget during first 4 weeks of launch.
- P95 request latency for the feature path within target SLO (example target: <= 300ms) and tail latency stable (P99 regressions flagged early).
- Zero customer-impacting incidents requiring >30m escalation during initial rollout window via pre-validated fallback policy.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- New feature endpoints and any change to routing that materially changes traffic patterns to model-serving cluster(s).
- Downstream dependencies: cache tier, DB replicas, model-serving pool (GPU), edge routing.
- Excludes backend refactors that do not alter public routes or capacity footprint.

Key stakeholders and owners:
- Feature PM: Sofia Patel — product readiness, acceptance criteria, customer comms
- Feature Eng Lead: Liam O'Connor — implementation, feature flags, rollout gating
- SRE Lead: Maya Chen — SLO definition, incident anchor, escalation
- Observability Owner: Aidan Brooks — dashboards, alerts, synthetic checks
- Infra/Platform: Grace Huang — capacity reservations, autoscale policy, deployment config
- Solutions/CS contact: Diego Morales — customer-facing escalation and comms
- Security/Compliance (as required) — review if feature touches PII or regulated data

Success criteria (pass/fail signals):
- Pass: All synthetic checks green at canary volume and stable for 48h; error budget burn rate under 0.5x expected; no Sev2/Sev1 incidents attributable to the feature in first 72h of ramp beyond routine alerts that are handled by oncall.
- Fail: Sustained error budget burn >1.0x for 2 consecutive 30m windows, P95 regression >20% vs baseline, or any customer-impacting rollback is required.

SLOs and service-level objectives (feature-level):
- Define one canonical SLO for the feature route (examples below — store in SLO registry):
  - Availability (success rate): 99.9% over 30d for feature-route (responses with 2xx/3xx).
  - Latency: P95 <= 300ms over 7d rolling during steady state.
  - Error budget window and burn policy: feature has a separate budget for first 30d; SRE sets burn thresholds to trigger throttle or rollback.
Note: keep SLO count minimal — prefer one availability SLO and one latency SLO for the feature path.

Timeline: microcycles and milestones (recommended 8-week example)
- Week -4 to -2 (Discovery & definition): define feature SLOs, list critical downstream dependencies, sketch load profile (expected QPS and burst), identify experiments and rollback criteria.
- Week -2 to 0 (Prepare & instrument): runbook draft, dashboards created, synthetic checks authored, smoke tests, capacity reservation request filed, simple load tests on staging.
- Week 0 (Canary small %): deploy behind feature flag to 1% of traffic; SRE observes burn, run synthetic + chaos probe; decide go/no-go after 48h.
- Week 1 (Ramped canary): increase to 10% if metrics stable for 48–72h; run more aggressive load and tail-latency probes; enable additional alerts.
- Week 2–3 (Gradual ramp): 25% -> 50% with monitoring and manual checkpoints; finish customer communications for GA.
- Week 4 (GA): full ramp to 100% with post-launch review at day 7 and 30.

Workstreams and primary tasks:
1) SLO & policy (owner: SRE Lead)
   - Draft SLO statements and labels for telemetry ingestion.
   - Register SLO in SLO registry and link to runbook.
   - Define automated actions: throttle route, revert flag, or spill to fallback model when burn thresholds exceed defined windows.
2) Observability (owner: Observability Owner)
   - Build dashboards: feature-route error, P95/P99, error-class breakdown, downstream latency map.
   - Synthetic tests: happy path + failure modes (cache miss, DB high-latency, model cold-start).
   - Alert tuning: low-noise alerts for ops, high-sensitivity for canary.
3) Capacity & Load (owner: Infra/Platform)
   - Reserve capacity (Dedicated or burst pool) for first 7 days; scale policy validated in staging.
   - Run capacity tests: 1.5x expected peak QPS and long-tail stress tests.
4) Runbooks & Playbooks (owner: SRE Lead + Eng Lead)
   - Create feature-specific runbook with rollback steps, mitigation steps (circuit-breaker, rate-limit), and postmortem template.
   - Link to paging escalation matrix and oncall rotations.
5) Release & Flagging (owner: Feature Eng Lead)
   - Implement progressive flag with explicit gating checks in CI.
   - Provide a one-click rollback button in deployment console where possible.
6) Customer comms & CS play (owner: Product + Solutions)
   - Pre-launch notice to affected customers, post-launch status templates, and a fast-path for customer escalations.
7) Security & Compliance checkpoint (owner: Security)
   - Quick review for dataflows; signoff required before canary.

Operational checklists (pre-canary):
- SLOs registered and linked to alerts.
- Dashboards visible to all stakeholders and pinned in #reliability-launch-coord.
- Synthetic checks green in staging for 72h.
- Capacity reservation and autoscaling validated under 1.5x load.
- Rollback procedure validated via rehearsed dry-run.
- Customer comms drafted and approved.

Runbook excerpt (short):
- Symptom: sudden P95 increase >20% vs baseline and error rate >0.5%
- Immediate action (0–15m): remove feature flag from traffic, switch traffic to fallback route, escalate to SRE lead and infra.
- Triage (15–60m): capture traces, hit-run synthetic test, inspect model-serving queue length and GPU memory metrics, decide rollback or further mitigation.
- Post-incident (day 0–7): collect timeline, runbook adherence check, postmortem assign.

Escalation matrix:
- Pager -> oncall SRE -> SRE Lead -> Eng Lead -> Product PM -> Exec on-call if Sev1 continues beyond 60m.

Communication plan:
- Pre-launch: one-week and one-day reminders to stakeholders, list of watch windows (UTC).
- During canary: live dashboard link + spot-check updates at 8h, 24h, 48h.
- If anomalies: immediate Slack ping to #reliability-launch-coord and update ticket REL-3210.
- Post-launch: 7-day stability note and 30-day wrap review with lessons learned.

Risk register (top risks):
- Downstream DB read replicas not catching up under burst -> mitigation: circuit-breaker + read-fallthrough to cached copy.
- Model cold-starts on GPU causing P99 spikes -> mitigation: pre-warm pool and shorter cold-start synthetic probes.
- Alert noise causing operator fatigue -> mitigation: tune alert thresholds and use canary-only alert routing.

Open questions (to resolve in discovery):
- Does this feature require a separate SLO budget or should it consume service-wide budget? (Decision by SRE + Product)
- What fallback quality threshold (model accuracy/latency) is acceptable for spillover?
- Are there regulatory requirements for customer notification for the feature rollout?

Action items (owner, due dates):
- SRE: create SLO draft and SLO registry entry (owner: Maya Chen) — due 2026-11-22.
- Observability: create canary dashboard and 3 synthetic checks (owner: Aidan Brooks) — due 2026-11-29.
- Infra: capacity reservation + autoscale test plan (owner: Grace Huang) — due 2026-12-01.
- Eng: implement feature flag with rollback hook (owner: Liam O'Connor) — due 2026-12-05.
- Product: customer comms templates (owner: Sofia Patel) — due 2026-12-05.

Metrics to monitor during rollout (live):
- Feature-route success rate, 1m and 5m error rates.
- P95 and P99 latency for feature path and for top 3 downstream calls.
- Error budget burn rate (1h / 24h windows).
- Queue lengths and GPU utilization for model-serving pools.
- Cache hit ratio for feature-specific cache keys.

Post-launch retro checklist (day 7 & day 30):
- Confirm runbook steps were followed; update runbook where gaps are found.
- Reconcile SLO performance vs. target; adjust SLO or rollout policy if required.
- Document one operational improvement and one product tuning item.

Appendix: quick links and templates
- Runbook template: confluence:RUNBOOK-TEMPLATE-02
- SLO registration guide: confluence:SLO-WORKFLOW-10
- Jira epic for this launch: JIRA:REL-3210

Notes to self / working items (informal):
- Consider a short chaos test (kill 1% of model-serving pods) during canary to validate fallback.
- Might want a temporary increased retention of traces for 72h post-canary for easier triage.
- We should coordinate with Dedicated team for reserved GPU pool naming convention.

If you’re reading this and want to take ownership of a line item, drop a comment in the doc and ping @Maya on Slack.
